title.zh: 卷二 本紀第二 武帝中
title.raw: 卷二 本紀第二 武帝中 Volume 2 Annals 2: Emperor Wu 2

sentences.zh: 七年正月己未，振旅于京師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, on the day jiwei, he led the army back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year (411), on the day jiwei, Gaozu marched his troops back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 改授大將軍、揚州牧，給班劍二十人，本官悉如故，固辭。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Grand General and Governor of Yangzhou, granted twenty ceremonial swords, and all his original offices were left unchanged; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The court offered him Grand General and Governor of Yangzhou, with twenty ceremonial swords and all his old posts unchanged. He refused.

sentences.zh: 凡南北征伐戰亡者，並列上賻贈。

translations.literal: All who had died in battle on the northern and southern campaigns were to be listed and presented for funeral subsidies.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a full list of those killed in the northern and southern campaigns, with funeral grants for each.

sentences.zh: 尸喪未反，遣主帥迎接，致還本土。

translations.literal: Where the dead had not yet been brought back, he sent the commanders to receive them and return them to their native districts.
translations.idiomatic: Where bodies had not yet come home, he sent the field commanders to escort them back to their home districts.

sentences.zh: 二月，盧循至番禺，為孫季高所破，收餘眾南走。

translations.literal: In the second month, Lu Xun reached Panyu, was defeated by Sun Jigao, gathered his remaining forces, and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Lu Xun reached Panyu. Sun Jigao defeated him; he gathered what was left of his army and fled south.

sentences.zh: 劉藩、孟懷玉斬徐道覆于始興。

translations.literal: Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu beheaded Xu Daofu at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: At Shixing, Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu beheaded Xu Daofu.

sentences.zh: 晉自中興以來，治綱大弛，權門并兼，強弱相凌，百姓流離，不得保其產業。

translations.literal: Since the Jin restoration, the bonds of governance had greatly slackened; powerful houses annexed one another, the strong bullied the weak, and the common people were displaced and could not keep their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin court moved south, government had grown lax. Great families swallowed their neighbors, the strong preyed on the weak, and ordinary people lost their homes and could not hold on to their land.

sentences.zh: 桓玄頗欲釐改，竟不能行。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan had wished somewhat to reform this, but in the end could not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan had tried to set things right, but never managed to.

sentences.zh: 公既作輔，大示軌則，豪強肅然，遠近知禁。

translations.literal: Once Gaozu had become regent, he displayed great norms; the powerful were awed into order, and near and far learned what was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaozu took power as regent, he laid down clear rules. The mighty fell silent, and everyone, near and far, knew the law.

sentences.zh: 至是會稽餘姚虞亮復藏匿亡命千餘人。

translations.literal: At this time Yu Liang of Yuyao in Kuaiji again harbored more than a thousand fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yu Liang of Yuyao in Kuaiji was again sheltering over a thousand fugitives.

sentences.zh: 公誅亮，免會稽內史司馬休之。

translations.literal: Gaozu executed Liang and dismissed Sima Xiuzhi, Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had Liang executed and removed Sima Xiuzhi as Interior Minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 天子又申前命，公固辭。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again pressed the earlier appointment upon him, and Gaozu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed the earlier honors on him again. Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 於是改授太尉、中書監，乃受命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was reassigned as Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and then accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and this time he accepted.

sentences.zh: 奉送黃鉞，解冀州。

translations.literal: The court presented the yellow battle-axe, and he relinquished Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent him the yellow battle-axe; he gave up Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史杜慧度斬盧循，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiaozhou Du Huidu beheaded Lu Xun and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huidu, Inspector of Jiaozhou, killed Lu Xun and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是諸州郡所遣秀才、孝廉，多非其人，公表天子，申明舊制，依舊策試。

translations.literal: Previously the Recommended Scholars and Filial and Incorrupt candidates sent up by the provinces and commanderies had often not been fit men; Gaozu memorialized the Son of Heaven, clarifying the old regulations and restoring the written examinations as before.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial nominees for office had often been unworthy. Gaozu petitioned the throne to restore the old examination system.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍、荊州刺史道規疾患求歸，八年四月，改授豫州刺史，以後將軍、豫州刺史劉毅代之。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou Daogui, ill, asked to return; in the fourth month of the eighth year he was reassigned as Inspector of Yuzhou, and Rear General and Inspector of Yuzhou Liu Yi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, fell ill and asked to come home. In the fourth month of the eighth year (412) he was made Inspector of Yuzhou; Liu Yi, Rear General and Inspector of Yuzhou, took his place in Jing.

sentences.zh: 毅與公俱舉大義，興復晉室，自謂京城、廣陵，功業足以相抗。

translations.literal: Yi had raised the great cause together with Gaozu and restored the Jin house; he considered that his achievements at the capital and at Guangling were enough to rival Gaozu's.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had joined Gaozu in restoring the Jin dynasty and thought his deeds at the capital and at Guangling matched Gaozu's own.

sentences.zh: 雖權事推公，而心不服也。

translations.literal: Though in power he deferred to Gaozu, in his heart he was not content.
translations.idiomatic: He yielded to Gaozu in public, but in his heart he would not submit.

sentences.zh: 毅既有雄才大志，厚自矜許，朝士素望者多歸之。

translations.literal: Yi possessed great talent and high ambition and thought highly of himself; many courtiers of long-standing repute turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was talented, ambitious, and vain. Many senior officials looked to him instead.

sentences.zh: 與尚書僕射謝混、丹陽尹郗僧施並深相結。

translations.literal: He was deeply allied with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Hun and Chief of Danyang Xi Sengshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Xie Hun, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Xi Sengshi, Chief of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 及西鎮江陵，豫州舊府，多割以自隨，請僧施為南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: When he went west to Jiangling, the old offices of Yuzhou were largely carved up for his own use, and he requested that Sengshi be made Commander Who Pacifies the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held Jiangling in the west, he took over much of the old Yuzhou establishment and asked that Sengshi be made Commander Who Pacifies the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 既知毅不能居下，終為異端，密圖之。

translations.literal: Knowing that Yi could not remain subordinate and would in the end become a rebel, he secretly laid plans against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu saw that Yi would never stay below him and would turn rebel; he began to plot in secret.

sentences.zh: 毅至西，稱疾篤，表求從弟兗州刺史藩以為副貳，偽許焉。

translations.literal: When Yi reached the west he claimed grave illness and memorialized, asking that his younger cousin Fan, Inspector of Yanzhou, be made his deputy; this was falsely granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reached the west, claimed to be gravely ill, and asked that his cousin Fan, Inspector of Yanzhou, be made his deputy. Gaozu pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 九月，藩入朝，公命收藩及謝混，並於獄賜死。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, when Fan entered court, Gaozu ordered Fan and Xie Hun seized and both were granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Fan came to court. Gaozu had him and Xie Hun arrested and executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 自表討毅。

translations.literal: He himself memorialized to campaign against Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to take the field against Yi.

sentences.zh: 又假黃鉞，率諸軍西征。

translations.literal: He was also lent the yellow battle-axe and led the armies west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the yellow battle-axe and marched west at the head of the armies.

sentences.zh: 以前鎮軍將軍司馬休之為平西將軍、荊州刺史，兗州刺史道憐鎮丹徒，豫州刺史諸葛長民監太尉留府事，加太尉司馬、丹陽尹劉穆之建威將軍，配以實力。

translations.literal: Former General Who Guards the Army Sima Xiuzhi was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Inspector of Yanzhou Daoling garrisoned Dantu; Inspector of Yuzhou Zhuge Changmin oversaw the Grand Commandant's headquarters; and Grand Commandant Marshal and Chief of Danyang Liu Muzhi was made General Who Establishes Might, each posted with real force.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Daoling held Dantu; Changmin ran the capital in Gaozu's absence; Muzhi was made General Who Establishes Might—all with real troops behind them.

sentences.zh: 壬午，發自京師。

translations.literal: On the day renwu he set out from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu he marched out from the capital.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍王鎮惡、龍驤將軍蒯恩前襲江陵。

translations.literal: He sent Staff Officer Wang Zhen'e and Dragon-Chariot General Kuai En ahead to strike Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Zhen'e and Kuai En ahead to take Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十月，鎮惡剋江陵，毅及黨與皆伏誅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Zhen'e took Jiangling; Yi and his partisans were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhen'e took Jiangling. Yi and his followers were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯，公至江陵，下書曰：

translations.literal: On the day jimao of the eleventh month, Gaozu reached Jiangling and issued a proclamation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao in the eleventh month Gaozu reached Jiangling and issued a proclamation:

sentences.zh: 夫去弊拯民，必存簡恕，捨網修綱，雖煩易理。

translations.literal: "To remove abuses and save the people, one must preserve simplicity and forbearance; to cast aside the net and repair the cords, though troublesome, is easy to justify in principle."
translations.idiomatic: "To cure abuses and help the people, government must stay simple and humane. Tightening the law after years of disorder is hard work, but it is the right course."

sentences.zh: 江、荊彫殘，刑政多闕，頃年事故，綏撫未週。

translations.literal: Jiang and Jing were wasted and maimed; penal administration had many gaps; in recent years, because of upheaval, pacification had not been thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and Jing were devastated; justice was patchy; years of turmoil had left the region half-settled.

sentences.zh: 遂令百姓疲匱，歲月滋甚，財傷役困，慮不幸生。

translations.literal: Thus the common people grew exhausted and impoverished, month by month the harm deepened, wealth was injured and corvée labor distressed, and I feared misfortune might arise.
translations.idiomatic: The people grew poorer every month, taxes and labor broke them, and I feared worse would follow.

sentences.zh: 凋殘之餘，而不減舊，刻剝徵求，不循政道。

translations.literal: On what remained of the wasted land, levies were not reduced from old levels; exactions and requisitions did not follow the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Even on ruined ground the old levies stood. Officials squeezed the people without regard to law.

sentences.zh: 宰莅之司，或非良榦，未能菲躬儉，[1]苟求盈給，積習生常，漸不知改。

translations.literal: The officials who presided over districts were not always capable men; they could not restrain themselves in frugality, [1] but sought only to fill quotas; accumulated habit became custom, and gradually they no longer knew how to change.
translations.idiomatic: Many local magistrates were unfit. They would not live plainly [1] but chased every quota until waste became habit and reform seemed impossible.

sentences.zh: 近因戎役，來涉二州，踐境親民，愈見其瘼，思欲振其所急，卹其所苦。

translations.literal: Recently, because of the military campaign, I have come to these two provinces; treading the borders and facing the people, I have seen their afflictions all the more clearly, and I wish to rouse what is urgent and relieve what is bitter.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign has brought me into both provinces. Seeing the people myself, I know their distress and mean to ease what hurts them most.

sentences.zh: 凡租稅調役，悉宜以見戶為正。

translations.literal: All rent, tax, and corvée levies should be based entirely on registered households as they stand.
translations.idiomatic: All rent, tax, and labor duties shall be assessed only on actual registered households.

sentences.zh: 州郡縣屯田池塞，諸非軍國所資，利入守宰者，今一切除之。

translations.literal: Garrison fields, ponds, and passes in the provinces, commanderies, and counties—whatever did not serve military or state needs but whose profits went to the guarding magistrates—are now all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial garrison farms, ponds, and toll stations that served private profit rather than the army or the state are abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 州郡縣吏，皆依尚書定制實戶置。

translations.literal: Officials in the provinces, commanderies, and counties shall all be appointed according to the Masters of Writing's fixed quotas for actual households.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial, commandery, and county staffs shall be set only at the numbers the Masters of Writing allow for real households.

sentences.zh: 臺調癸卯梓材，庚子皮毛，可悉停省，別量所出。

translations.literal: The court requisitions of guimao timber and gengzi hides may all be halted and reduced; other sources shall be measured instead.
translations.idiomatic: Court demands for guimao timber and gengzi hides are suspended; other supplies will be found.

sentences.zh: 巴陵均折度支，依舊兵運。

translations.literal: The Ba-ling equalization and expenditure office shall follow the old military transport rules.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba-ling equalization office shall return to the old military transport system.

sentences.zh: 原五歲刑已下。

translations.literal: Pardon all punishments of five years or less.
translations.idiomatic: All sentences of five years or less are pardoned.

sentences.zh: 凡所質錄賊家餘口，亦悉原放。

translations.literal: All dependents of rebel households held as pledges are likewise to be released.
translations.idiomatic: Dependents taken hostage from rebel families are also freed.

sentences.zh: 以荊州十郡為湘州，公乃進督。

translations.literal: Ten commanderies of Jingzhou were made into Xiangzhou, and Gaozu then advanced as supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Ten commanderies of Jing were split off as Xiang province, and Gaozu took overall supervision.

sentences.zh: [2]以西陽太守朱齡石為益州刺史，率眾伐蜀。

translations.literal: [2] Administrator of Xiyang Zhu Lingshi was made Inspector of Yizhou and led the armies to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Zhu Lingshi, Administrator of Xiyang, was made Inspector of Yizhou and marched against Shu.

sentences.zh: 進公太傅、揚州牧，加羽葆鼓吹，班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Gaozu was promoted to Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with feathered canopy, drums, and whistles, and twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with imperial music and twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 九年二月乙丑，公至自江陵。

translations.literal: On the day yichou of the second month of the ninth year, Gaozu returned from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou in the second month of the ninth year (413) Gaozu returned from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初諸葛長民貪淫驕橫，為士民所患苦，公以其同大義，優容之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhuge Changmin had been greedy, licentious, arrogant, and overbearing, a affliction to scholars and commoners; Gaozu, because he had shared the great cause, treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin had long been greedy, brutal, and hated by the people. Gaozu had tolerated him because they had fought together for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 劉毅既誅，長民謂所親曰：「昔年醢彭越，今年誅韓信，禍其至矣。

translations.literal: After Liu Yi was executed, Changmin said to those close to him: "Last year they minced Peng Yue; this year they kill Han Xin—disaster is upon me.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi died, Changmin told his intimates, "Last year Peng Yue was boiled; this year Han Xin is killed. My turn is coming.

sentences.zh: 」將謀作亂。

translations.literal: " He was about to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " He began to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 公克期至京邑，而每淹留不進。

translations.literal: Gaozu had set a date to reach the capital, yet each day he delayed and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had named a day to reach the capital, but lingered on the road.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下頻日奉候於新亭，長民亦驟出。

translations.literal: From the Three Dukes down, for days on end they went to wait upon him at Xinting; Changmin too came out repeatedly in haste.
translations.idiomatic: For days the highest officials waited on him at Xinting. Changmin kept hurrying out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 既而公輕舟密至，已還東府矣。

translations.literal: Presently Gaozu came secretly in a light boat and was already back at the eastern headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Then Gaozu slipped in by light boat and was already back at his eastern headquarters.

sentences.zh: 長民到門。

translations.literal: Changmin came to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin came to the gate.

sentences.zh: 引前，卻人閑語，凡平生於長民所不盡者，皆與及之。

translations.literal: Gaozu drew him forward, dismissed the attendants, and in private conversation went over everything in their lives that he had never yet said to Changmin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu brought him in, sent everyone else away, and spoke with him at length about everything he had never yet said between them.

sentences.zh: 長民甚說。

translations.literal: Changmin was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin was delighted.

sentences.zh: 已密命左右壯士丁旿等自幔後出，於坐拉焉。

translations.literal: He had already secretly ordered the strong men at his side, Ding Wu and the rest, to come out from behind the curtain and seize him where he sat.
translations.idiomatic: He had already told his strongmen, Ding Wu and the rest, to slip out from behind the curtain and seize him in his seat.

sentences.zh: 長民墜牀，又於地毆之，死於牀側。

translations.literal: Changmin fell from the couch; they beat him again on the ground, and he died beside the couch.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin fell from the couch. They beat him on the floor until he died beside it.

sentences.zh: 輿尸付廷尉。

translations.literal: His body was placed in a cart and handed over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The body was carted to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 并誅其弟黎民。

translations.literal: His younger brother Limin was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Limin was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 旿驍勇有氣力，時人為之語曰：「勿跋扈，付丁旿。」

translations.literal: Wu was fierce and brave and full of strength; at the time people made a saying of it: "Do not act the bully—hand it to Ding Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Wu was famously fierce. People said, "Don't play the tyrant—leave it to Ding Wu."

sentences.zh: 先是山湖川澤，皆為豪強所專，小民薪採漁釣，皆責稅直，至是禁斷之。

translations.literal: Previously, mountains, lakes, rivers, and marshes had all been monopolized by the powerful; common people gathering firewood, fishing, or cutting reeds all paid a tax; now this was forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families had seized lakes, rivers, and hills; even firewood and fishing carried a fee. That was now forbidden.

sentences.zh: 時民居未一，公表曰：

translations.literal: At the time the people were not yet settled in one place; Gaozu memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The people were still unsettled. Gaozu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞先王制治，九土攸序，分境畫疆，各安其居。

translations.literal: I have heard that the former kings in establishing order arranged the nine domains in sequence, divided borders and drew boundaries, and each kept to his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings ordered the realm by fixing borders so that each people could dwell in peace.

sentences.zh: 在昔盛世，人無遷業，故井田之制，三代以隆。

translations.literal: In past ages of flourishing rule, men did not change their occupations; thus the well-field system flourished through the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In great ages no one left his trade; that is why the well-field system lasted through the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 秦革斯政，漢遂不改，富強兼并，於是為弊。

translations.literal: Qin overturned this policy; Han did not change it, and the strong annexed the rich—thus the abuse arose.
translations.idiomatic: Qin abolished that order; Han kept the change, and the strong swallowed the weak.

sentences.zh: 然九服弗擾，所託成舊，在漢西京，大遷田、景之族，以實關中，即以三輔為鄉閭，不復係之於齊、楚。

translations.literal: Yet the nine domains were not disturbed; what they relied on remained the old. In the Western Han capital, the clans of Tian and Jing were moved on a great scale to fill Guanzhong, and the Three Metropolises became their native hamlets, no longer tied to Qi and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Still the realm held together because people kept their roots. In Western Han the Tian and Jing clans were moved en masse into Guanzhong; the capital districts became home and they were cut off from Qi and Chu.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉播越，爰託淮、海，朝有匡復之算，民懷思本之心，經略之圖，日不暇給。

translations.literal: From the Yongjia turmoil onward, the court entrusted itself to the Huai and the sea; the court had plans to restore the realm, and the people cherished the wish to return to their roots; schemes of strategy left no day free.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongjia the court fled to the Huai and the sea. All wanted restoration, and the people longed for home, but war left no day for civil rule.

sentences.zh: 是以寧民綏治，猶有未遑。

translations.literal: Thus in settling the people and pacifying rule, there was still no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Peaceful settlement had to wait.

sentences.zh: 及至大司馬桓溫，以民無定本，傷治為深，庚戌土斷，以一其業。

translations.literal: When Grand Marshal Huan Wen saw that the people had no fixed base and that harm to governance lay deep therein, in the year gengxu he carried out the land register to unify their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Huan Wen saw that people had no fixed domicile and government suffered for it, he carried out the gengxu land register in 365 to give everyone a single legal home.

sentences.zh: 于時財阜國豐，實由於此。

translations.literal: At that time wealth flourished and the state was rich—this was truly owing to that measure.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury grew rich because of it.

sentences.zh: 自茲迄今，彌歷年載，畫一之制，漸用頹弛。

translations.literal: From then until now, many years have passed; the unified system has gradually fallen into decay.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the unified system had slowly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 雜居流寓，閭伍弗修，王化所以未純，民瘼所以猶在。

translations.literal: Mixed residence and floating registration, neighborhood registers not kept in order—the royal transformation was therefore not pure, and the people's afflictions therefore remained.
translations.idiomatic: Migrants and false registers broke the wards; government never fully took hold, and the people's misery remained.

sentences.zh: 臣荷重任，恥責實深，自非改調解張，無以濟治。

translations.literal: I bear a heavy commission and am deeply ashamed of the gap between charge and result; unless I change the registers and loosen the bonds, I cannot bring order.
translations.idiomatic: I hold great power and am ashamed that rule still fails. Without fixing the registers I cannot govern.

sentences.zh: 夫人情滯常，難與慮始，所謂父母之邦以為桑梓者，誠以生焉終焉，敬愛所託耳。

translations.literal: Human feeling clings to the constant and finds it hard to plan at the beginning; what is called taking one's native district as one's mulberry tree is truly because one is born and dies there and the object of reverent love is entrusted there.
translations.idiomatic: People cling to habit and hate sudden change. They call their home a mulberry tree because they are born and buried there and their loyalty belongs there.

sentences.zh: 今所居累世，墳壟成行，敬恭之誠，豈不與事而至。

translations.literal: Where they now dwell for generations, graves and mounds stand in rows; the sincerity of reverence—how could it fail to attend upon the matter when it comes?
translations.idiomatic: Families have lived in one place for generations; their graves line the fields. How could they not care when the state asks them to move?

sentences.zh: 請準庚戌土斷之科，庶子本所弘，稍與事著。

translations.literal: I ask that the gengxu land-register statute be applied, so that the intent to honor native roots may be broadly carried out and may gradually show in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the gengxu land register be enforced again, so respect for native roots may guide policy.

sentences.zh: 然後率之以仁義，鼓之以威武，超大江而跨黃河，撫九州而復舊土，則戀本之志，乃速申於當年，[3]在始暫勤，要終所以能易。

translations.literal: Then, leading them with benevolence and righteousness and rousing them with martial might, crossing the great river and spanning the Yellow River, comforting the nine provinces and recovering the old lands—then the wish to cherish one's roots would quickly be fulfilled in that year, [3] a brief hardship at the start, but in the end the change could be made easy.
translations.idiomatic: Then, with benevolence and force together, we may cross the Yangtze and Yellow River, recover the north, and give every man his home again. [3] The pain at first will be brief; in the end the change will be easy.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，垂矜萬民，憐其所失，永懷鴻雁之詩，思隆中興之業。

translations.literal: Bow your head, Your Majesty, pitying the myriad people, cherishing what they have lost, ever keeping in mind the ode of the wild geese, thinking to exalt the enterprise of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pities the people, remembers what they have lost, and keeps the ode of the wild geese in mind, longing to restore the realm.

sentences.zh: 既委臣以國重，期臣以寧濟，若所啟合允，請付外施行。

translations.literal: Having entrusted me with the weight of the state and expecting me to bring peace, if what I propose is fitting, I ask that it be sent out and put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: You have charged me with the realm and expect peace from me. If this plan is sound, let it be carried out.

sentences.zh: 於是依界土斷，唯徐、兗、青三州居晉陵者，不在斷例。

translations.literal: Thereupon land was registered according to boundaries; only those in Jinling from Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces were outside the statute.
translations.idiomatic: Land was then registered by district. Only households of Xu, Yan, and Qing living in Jinling were exempt.

sentences.zh: 諸流寓郡縣，多被併省。

translations.literal: Many of the floating commanderies and counties were merged or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Many refugee commanderies and counties were merged or abolished.

sentences.zh: 以公領鎮西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 公固讓太傅、州牧及班劍，奉還黃鉞。

translations.literal: Gaozu firmly declined Grand Tutor, Governor of the province, and the ceremonial swords, and returned the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused the Grand Tutorship, the governorship, and the ceremonial swords, and sent back the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 七月，朱齡石平蜀，斬偽蜀王譙縱，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Zhu Lingshi pacified Shu, beheaded the false King of Shu Qiao Zong, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhu Lingshi conquered Shu, killed the pretender Qiao Zong, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，封公次子義真為桂陽縣公，以賞平齊及定盧循也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Gaozu's second son Yizhen was enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyang, to reward the pacification of Qi and the defeat of Lu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Gaozu's second son Yizhen was made Duke of Guiyang, rewarding the conquest of Qi and the defeat of Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 天子重申前命，授公太傅、揚州牧，加羽葆、鼓吹、班劍二十人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again pressed the earlier appointment: Gaozu was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with feathered canopy, drums, whistles, and twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again pressed the old honors on him: Grand Tutor, Governor of Yangzhou, imperial music, and twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 將吏百餘敦勸，乃受羽葆、鼓吹、班劍，餘固辭。

translations.literal: More than a hundred officers urged him earnestly; only then did he accept the feathered canopy, drums, whistles, and ceremonial swords; the rest he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred officers begged him to accept. He took the music and swords but refused the rest.

sentences.zh: 十年，息民簡役。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he gave the people rest and simplified corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (414) he eased burdens on the people and cut labor duties.

sentences.zh: 築東府，起府舍。

translations.literal: He built the eastern headquarters and raised the official residences.
translations.idiomatic: He built the eastern headquarters and its offices.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍、荊州刺史司馬休之，宗室之重，又得江漢人心，公疑其有異志，而休之兄子譙王文思在京師，招集輕俠，公執文思送還休之，令自為其所。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou Sima Xiuzhi was a man of weight in the imperial clan and had won the hearts of the Jiang and Han regions; Gaozu suspected he harbored a different intent. Xiuzhi's elder brother's son, the Marquis of Qiao Wen Si, was in the capital gathering daredevils; Gaozu seized Wen Si and sent him back to Xiuzhi, telling him to deal with the matter himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, was a prince of the blood with a following in Jiang and Han. Gaozu distrusted him. Xiuzhi's nephew Wen Si was in the capital gathering ruffians; Gaozu arrested Wen Si and sent him to Xiuzhi to punish as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 休之表廢文思，并與公書陳謝。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized to dismiss Wen Si and also wrote Gaozu a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi memorialized to disown Wen Si and wrote Gaozu to apologize.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，公收休之子文寶、兄子文祖，並於獄賜死，率眾軍西討。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, Gaozu seized Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and his brother's son Wenzu and granted them death in prison, then led the armies west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year (415) Gaozu had Wenbao and Wenzu executed in prison and marched west.

sentences.zh: 復加黃鉞，[4]領荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again given the yellow battle-axe [4] and took charge as Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again given the yellow battle-axe [4] and made Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，發京師，以中軍將軍道憐監留府事。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi he set out from the capital; Central Army General Daoling oversaw the headquarters left behind.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi he left the capital. Daoling ran affairs at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 休之上表自陳曰：

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized in his own person, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi submitted a personal memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞運不常一，治亂代有，陽九既謝，圮終則泰。

translations.literal: I have heard that fortune is not constant, order and disorder succeed each other in turn; when the yang ninth calamity has passed, collapse at the end gives way to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune never stays the same; order and chaos take turns. When the worst is past, ruin gives way to renewal.

sentences.zh: 昔篡臣肆逆，皇綱絕紐，卜世未改，[5]鼎祚再隆。

translations.literal: In former days the usurping minister ran riot, the imperial cords were severed, the allotted age was not yet changed, [5] and the sacred vessel was raised a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Once a usurper seized power and the dynasty seemed dead, yet the throne was restored [5] and the mandate lived again.

sentences.zh: 太尉臣裕威武明斷，道建義旗，除蕩元凶，皇居反正。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Liu Yu was martially awesome and brilliantly decisive; he raised the banner of righteousness, swept away the chief villain, and restored the imperial palace to right order.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Liu Yu was fierce and clear-sighted. He raised the righteous standard, destroyed the usurper, and brought the throne back to order.

sentences.zh: 布衣匹夫，匡復社稷，南剿盧循，北定廣固，千載以來，功無與等。

translations.literal: A man in plain cloth, a commoner, he restored the altars of state; in the south he destroyed Lu Xun, in the north he pacified Guanggu—in a thousand years no achievement has equaled his.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner in homespun restored the dynasty; he crushed Lu Xun in the south and took Guanggu in the north. In a thousand years no deed has matched his.

sentences.zh: 由是四海歸美，朝野推崇。

translations.literal: Thus all within the seas turned their praise to him; court and countryside alike exalted him.
translations.idiomatic: All the realm praised him; court and country alike held him up.

sentences.zh: 既位窮台牧，權傾人主，不能以道處功，恃寵驕溢。

translations.literal: Yet once he stood at the apex as regional governor and his power tilted as though he were the sovereign, he could not treat his merit with the Way but relied on favor and swelled with pride.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once he reached the summit as a frontier lord and bent power as if he were the ruler, he would not measure his merit by the Way and grew arrogant on imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 自以酬賞既極，便情在無上，刑戮逆濫，政用暴苛。

translations.literal: Thinking his rewards had reached their limit, his desire turned toward what lies above all; executions and punishments were perverse and excessive, and government was harsh and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Believing he had been rewarded to the full, he set his heart on what is above all. Punishments ran wild; rule turned savage and harsh.

sentences.zh: 問鼎之迹日彰，人臣之禮頓缺。

translations.literal: His designs on the throne grew daily clearer; the rites owed by a minister abruptly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: His intent to seize the throne showed clearer each day; a subject's proper rites were cast aside.

sentences.zh: 陛下四時膳御，觸事縣空，宮省供奉，十不一在。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's meals through the four seasons were left empty at every turn; of the palace's provisions scarcely one in ten remained.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's food through the year was stripped bare at every turn; scarcely one part in ten of the palace supply remained.

sentences.zh: 皇后寢疾之際，湯藥不周，手與家書，多所求告。

translations.literal: When the Empress lay ill, medicine was not provided in full; he handled family letters himself and made many demands.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress was ill, remedies were not supplied; he wrote private letters himself and pressed many requests.

sentences.zh: 皆是朝士共所聞見，莫不傷懷憤歎，口不敢言。

translations.literal: These are things the court gentlemen have all seen and heard; none failed to grieve and rage in their hearts, yet none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials have all seen and heard this; every heart grieves and burns, yet no mouth dares speak.

sentences.zh: 前揚州刺史元顯第五息法興，桓玄之釁，逃遠於外，王路既開，始得歸本。

translations.literal: The former Inspector of Yangzhou Yuan Xian's fifth son Faxiang, because of Huan Xuan's crimes, had fled far away; once the imperial road was open again, he was able to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Faxiang, fifth son of the former Yangzhou inspector Yuan Xian, fled far during Huan Xuan's rebellion; when the throne's road reopened, he could at last come home.

sentences.zh: 太傅之胤，絕而復興，凡在有懷，誰不感慶。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor's line, cut off and then revived—whoever harbored any feeling could fail to rejoice?
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor's house, dead and then restored—who with a heart would not rejoice?

sentences.zh: 裕吞噬之心，不避輕重，以法興聰敏明慧，必為民望所歸，芳蘭既茂，內懷憎惡，乃妄扇異言，無罪即戮。

translations.literal: Yu harbored a devouring heart and spared neither light nor heavy prey; because Faxiang was clever and bright and would surely win the people's regard, and because the fragrant orchid had flourished, Yu nursed hatred within and spread false charges, putting him to death though he was innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Yu swallowed all without scruple. Faxiang was clever and sure to win the people's love; the orchid had bloomed, and Yu hated it. He spread lies and killed a guiltless man.

sentences.zh: 大司馬臣德文及王妃公主，情計切逼，並狼狽請命。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal De Wen and the princesses of the royal house, pressed to extremity in their feelings and calculations, all pleaded for their lives in dismay.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal De Wen and the royal princesses, driven to desperation, all begged for their lives in anguish.

sentences.zh: 逆肆禍毒，誓不矜許，寃酷之痛，感動行路。

translations.literal: He wantonly poured out calamity and poison and swore never to show mercy; the pain of unjust cruelty moved those who passed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He poured out ruin and refused mercy; the agony of his injustice moved travelers on the road.

sentences.zh: 自以地卑位重，荷恩崇大，乃以庶孽與德文嫡婚，致茲非偶，實由威逼。

translations.literal: Thinking himself low in origin yet high in position, burdened with grace and greatly honored, he married his bastard son to De Wen's legitimate daughter—an ill-matched union in truth born of intimidation.
translations.idiomatic: Low-born yet high-placed, he owed great favor—and forced a bastard son on De Wen's legitimate daughter. The match was wrong; fear made it so.

sentences.zh: 故衞將軍劉毅、右將軍劉藩、前將軍諸葛長民、尚書僕射謝混、南蠻校尉郗僧施，或盛勳德胤，令望在身，皆社稷輔弼，協讚所寄，無罪無辜，一旦夷滅。

translations.literal: Former Defender Liu Yi, Right General Liu Fan, Forward General Zhuge Zhangmin, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Hun, and Pacification Commissioner for the Southern Man Xi Sengshi—some were men of towering merit and honored descent, others bore shining repute—all were pillars of the state, yet without guilt or crime they were annihilated in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, Liu Fan, Zhuge Zhangmin, Xie Hun, Xi Sengshi—men of great merit or bright name, pillars of the realm—all were destroyed in a day without crime.

sentences.zh: 猜忍之性，終古所希。

translations.literal: A suspicious and cruel nature—seldom seen through all ages.
translations.idiomatic: Such suspicion and cruelty are rare in all history.

sentences.zh: 臣自惟門戶衰破，賴之獲存，皇家所重，終古難匹。

translations.literal: I reflect that my house has declined and been shattered, and that only through him did I survive; what the imperial house has valued in me is unmatched through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: My clan was broken; only through him did I survive. What the throne has prized in my house has no equal in history.

sentences.zh: 是以公私歸馮，事盡祗順。

translations.literal: Therefore in public and private affairs all turned to him; in everything I showed utmost deference.
translations.idiomatic: So in public and private I leaned on him and obeyed in all things.

sentences.zh: 再授荊州，輒苦陳告，自以才弱位隆，不宜久荷分陝，屢求解任，必不見聽。

translations.literal: When Jing province was granted me again, I repeatedly memorialized in distress, thinking my talent slight and my rank exalted and that I ought not long bear the burden of the frontier; again and again I sought release but was never heard.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was given me again I begged to be relieved, saying my talent was slight and my rank too high for the frontier. I asked again and again; no one listened.

sentences.zh: 前經攜侍老母，半家俱西，凡諸子姪，悉留京輦。

translations.literal: Earlier I had gone west escorting my aged mother, half my household with me; all my sons and nephews I left in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier I took my old mother west, half my family with me; all my sons and nephews I left in the capital.

sentences.zh: 臣兄子譙王文思，雖年少常人，粗免咎悔，性好交遊，未知防遠，羣醜交構，為其風聲。

translations.literal: My brother's son Wen Si of Qiao, though young and an ordinary man, was largely free of blame; he loved to associate with others and did not know to guard against distant trouble. A pack of villains plotted together and made him their rumor.
translations.idiomatic: My brother's son Wen Si of Qiao was young and ordinary, mostly without fault. He loved company and did not guard against distant harm. Villains plotted and made him their tale.

sentences.zh: 裕遂翦戮人士，遠送文思。

translations.literal: Yu then cut down gentlemen and sent Wen Si far away.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then killed men of standing and sent Wen Si away.

sentences.zh: 臣順其此旨，表送章節，請廢文思，改襲大宗，遣息文寶送女東歸。

translations.literal: I complied with this intent, submitted the memorials, requested Wen Si's deposition, had him adopt the main line, and sent my son Wen Bao to escort our daughter eastward home.
translations.idiomatic: I followed this course: memorialized to depose Wen Si, shift the main line, and sent Wen Bao east with our daughter.

sentences.zh: 自謂推誠奉順，理不過此。

translations.literal: I thought my sincerity and submission could not go further than this.
translations.idiomatic: I believed my loyalty could go no further.

sentences.zh: 豈意裕苞藏禍心，遂見討伐，加惡文思，構生罪釁。

translations.literal: Who could have expected that Yu harbored a treacherous heart and would launch punitive action? He heaped further blame on Wen Si and fabricated crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Who knew Yu hid treachery and would attack? He piled crimes on Wen Si and forged guilt.

sentences.zh: 羣小之言，遠近噂𠴲，而臣純愚，闇信必謂不然。

translations.literal: The talk of petty men spread near and far in slander, yet I, being blunt and foolish, blind in faith, was sure it could not be so.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men's gossip ran everywhere, yet I, dull and trusting, was sure it was false.

sentences.zh: 尋臣府司馬張茂度狼狽東歸，南平太守檀範之復以此月三日委郡叛逆，尋有審問，東軍已上。

translations.literal: Soon my bureau's Marshal Zhang Maodu fled east in dismay; the Administrator of Nanping Tan Fanzhi likewise on the third of this month abandoned his commandery in rebellion. There are already inquiries, and the eastern army has marched.
translations.idiomatic: Soon my marshal Zhang Maodu fled east in panic; Nanping's Tan Fanzhi rebelled and left his post on the third. Inquiry followed; the eastern army has moved.

sentences.zh: 裕今此舉，非有怨憎，正以臣王室之幹，位居藩岳，時賢既盡，唯臣獨存，規以翦滅，成其篡殺。

translations.literal: Yu's present campaign is not born of private hatred; it is simply that I am a pillar of the royal house, standing as a frontier great, the worthy men of the age already destroyed and I alone remaining—he plans to cut me down and complete his usurpation and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Yu does not act from private hate. I am a royal pillar on the frontier; the worthy are gone and I alone remain. He means to cut me down and seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍臣宗之、青州刺史臣敬宣，並是裕所深忌憚，欲以次除蕩，然後傾移天日，於事可易。

translations.literal: Defense Commander Zongzhi and Inspector of Qingzhou Jing Xuan are both deeply envied and feared by Yu; he wishes to eliminate them in turn and only then shift the sun in heaven—then the affair will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi and Jing Xuan are both feared by Yu. He will remove them next, then turn the sky—then the deed will be easy.

sentences.zh: 今荊、雍義徒，不召而集，子來之眾，其會如林。

translations.literal: Now righteous followers in Jing and Yong assemble without being summoned; a host comes like children returning home, gathering thick as a forest.
translations.idiomatic: Now loyal men of Jing and Yong gather unbidden; they come like sons to a father, thick as a forest.

sentences.zh: 豈臣無德所能綏致，蓋七廟之靈，理貫幽顯。

translations.literal: How could my lack of virtue bring this about? It is the spirits of the seven temples—that principle runs through hidden and manifest alike.
translations.idiomatic: This is not my virtue—it is the ancestral spirits, whose power joins the seen and unseen.

sentences.zh: 輒授文思振武將軍、南郡太守，宗之子竟陵太守魯軌進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: I thereupon appointed Wen Si General Who Pacifies the Martial and Administrator of Nanjun; Zongzhi's son Gui, Administrator of Jingling, was advanced to General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: I made Wen Si General Who Pacifies the Martial and Nanjun's governor; Zongzhi's son Gui of Jingling became General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 臣今與宗之親御大眾，出據江津，案甲抗威，隨宜應赴。

translations.literal: I now, with Zongzhi, shall personally lead the great hosts, move out to hold the Yangzi ford, rest our armor and display our might, and respond as occasions require.
translations.idiomatic: I now lead the host with Zongzhi to the Yangzi crossing, armor ready, and will answer as need arises.

sentences.zh: 今絳旗所指，唯裕兄弟父子而已。

translations.literal: The red banners point today only at Yu and his brothers, fathers and sons.
translations.idiomatic: Our banners aim only at Yu and his kin—fathers and sons, brothers all.

sentences.zh: 須剋蕩寇逆，尋續馳聞。

translations.literal: When the bandits are swept away, further reports will follow quickly.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels are cleared, word will follow at once.

sentences.zh: 由臣輕弱，致裕凌橫，上慚俯愧，無以厝顏。

translations.literal: Because I am slight and weak, Yu has grown overbearing—shame weighs on me from above, and I have no face to show.
translations.idiomatic: Weak as I am, Yu has grown insolent. Shame bows my head; I cannot lift my face.

sentences.zh: 休之府錄事參軍韓延之，故吏也，有幹用才能。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's bureau Recorder Han Yanzhi was a former subordinate of his, a man of capacity and talent.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhi, Recorder on Xiuzhi's staff, was an old retainer, capable and able.

sentences.zh: 公未至江陵，密使與之書曰：「文思事源，遠近所知，去秋遣康之送還司馬君者，[6]推至公之極也。

translations.literal: Before Gaozu reached Jiangling he secretly sent him a letter, saying: "The source of the Wen Si affair is known far and near. Last autumn, when Kang was sent to return the Lord of Sima, [6] that was the utmost of fairness to you.
translations.idiomatic: Before Gaozu reached Jiangling he wrote Han Yanzhi in secret: "Everyone knows how the Wen Si affair began. Sending Kang back last autumn to return the Sima lord [6] was the utmost fairness on my part.

sentences.zh: 而了不遜愧，又無表疏。

translations.literal: Yet he showed no modest shame and submitted no memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he showed no shame and sent no memorial.

sentences.zh: 文思經正不反，此是天地之不容。

translations.literal: Wen Si, having received the classics, did not return—that is what heaven and earth cannot tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Si received the rites and would not return—that heaven and earth cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 吾受命西討，止其父子而已。

translations.literal: I have received command to campaign west and aim only at father and son.
translations.idiomatic: I march west on imperial order, and my target is only father and son.

sentences.zh: 彼土僑舊，為所驅逼，一無所問。

translations.literal: The émigrés and old families of that region, driven by force, will not be questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: The refugees and old families there, forced along, will not be questioned.

sentences.zh: 往年郗僧施、謝邵、任集之等，交構積歲，專為劉毅謀主，所以至此。

translations.literal: In former years Xi Sengshi, Xie Shao, Ren Jizhi, and others plotted for years, serving Liu Yi as chief strategist—that is how we came to this.
translations.idiomatic: For years Xi Sengshi, Xie Shao, Ren Jizhi, and others plotted for Liu Yi—that is how we came here.

sentences.zh: 卿等諸人，一時逼迫，本無纖釁。

translations.literal: You gentlemen were pressed for a time and originally had not the slightest fault.
translations.idiomatic: You were pressed for a time; you had no fault at all.

sentences.zh: 吾處懷期物，自有由來。

translations.literal: My mind toward men of promise has its reasons, long standing.
translations.idiomatic: My regard for men of promise is old and has its reasons.

sentences.zh: 今在近路，正是諸人歸身之日。

translations.literal: Now that I am on the near road, this is the day for you all to return to yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am near, this is the day to come back to yourselves.

sentences.zh: 若大軍登道，交鋒接刃，蘭艾吾誠不分。

translations.literal: If the great army takes the road and blades meet, I truly make no distinction between orchid and mugwort.
translations.idiomatic: If the army marches and swords cross, I will not spare orchid for mugwort.

sentences.zh: 故具示意，并示同懷諸人。

translations.literal: Therefore I set forth my meaning in full and show it also to others of like mind.
translations.idiomatic: So I state my meaning fully and show it to all who share your mind.

sentences.zh: 」延之報曰：

translations.literal: " Yanzhi replied:
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi replied:

sentences.zh: 承親率戎馬，遠履西畿，闔境士庶，莫不恇駭。

translations.literal: I have received that you personally lead armed horses and have come far into the western capital region; gentry and commoners throughout the circuit are all struck with fear.
translations.idiomatic: You lead your army deep into the west; every man in the region is terrified.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 莫知師出之名故也。

translations.literal: Because they do not know the reason the army has marched out.
translations.idiomatic: Because no one knows why the army has marched.

sentences.zh: 今辱來疏，始知以譙王前事，良增歎息。

translations.literal: Now, shamed by your letter, I first learn that it is because of the former affair of the Prince of Qiao—how greatly this adds to my sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter shames me; only now I learn it is over the Prince of Qiao—how it deepens my grief.

sentences.zh: 司馬平西體國忠貞，欵愛待物，當於古人中求耳。

translations.literal: The Sima, Pacifier of the West, embodies loyalty to the state and treats men with sincere affection; one must seek his like among the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifier of the West Sima embodies loyalty and treats men with open heart; seek his like among the ancients.

sentences.zh: 以君公有匡復之勳，家國蒙賴，推德委誠，每事詢仰。

translations.literal: Because you, my lord, have the merit of restoration, the house and state rely on you; you extend virtue and entrust sincerity, and in every matter he consulted and looked up to you.
translations.idiomatic: You restored the realm; the state relies on you. He trusted you in all things and looked up to you.

sentences.zh: 譙王往以微事見劾，猶自表遜位；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiao, when charged before with a small matter, still memorialized to yield his place;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qiao, charged once with a small fault, still memorialized to step down;

sentences.zh: 況以大過而當默然邪。

translations.literal: how much less could he remain silent when the fault was great?
translations.idiomatic: how could he stay silent when the fault was great?

sentences.zh: 但康之前言有所不盡，故重使胡道諮白所懷。

translations.literal: Only Kang's earlier words did not express everything fully, so Hu Daozi was again sent to declare what was in our hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's earlier words were incomplete, so Hu Daozi was sent again to speak our hearts.

sentences.zh: 道未及反，已奏表廢之，所不盡者命耳。

translations.literal: Dao had not yet returned when the memorial to depose him was already submitted—what was not expressed was only his fate.
translations.idiomatic: Dao had not returned when the memorial to depose him went up—only his fate was left unsaid.

sentences.zh: 推寄相與之懷，正當如此？

translations.literal: Is this how one treats the trust placed between us?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how you honor trust between us?

sentences.zh: 有何不可，便興兵戈。

translations.literal: What could not be done that you must raise arms?
translations.idiomatic: What could not be settled that you must draw swords?

sentences.zh: 自義旗秉權以來，四方方伯，誰敢不先相諮疇，而逕表天子邪。

translations.literal: Since the banner of righteousness took power, which regional lord has dared not consult first with his peers before memorializing the Son of Heaven directly?
translations.idiomatic: Since the righteous standard rose, which lord has dared memorial the throne without consulting his peers?

sentences.zh: 譙王為宰相所責，又表廢之，經正何歸，表使何因，可謂「欲加之罪，其無辭乎」！

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiao was reproached by the chief minister and again memorialized his deposition—where does rectitude lie, what cause for the memorial? One may say, "If you want to condemn a man, you can always find a charge"!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince was blamed by the chief minister and memorialized his own deposition—where is justice, what cause for the table? "Want guilt? You'll find words."

sentences.zh: 劉裕足下，海內之人，誰不見足下此心，而復欲欺誑國士！

translations.literal: Liu Yu, beneath your feet—all within the seas see your heart, yet you would deceive the men of the state again!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu—all the realm sees your heart, yet you would fool the state again!

sentences.zh: 天地所不容，在彼不在此矣。

translations.literal: What heaven and earth cannot tolerate lies there, not here.
translations.idiomatic: What heaven and earth cannot bear is on your side, not mine.

sentences.zh: 來示言「處懷期物，自有由來」。

translations.literal: Your letter says, "My mind toward men of promise has its reasons, long standing."
translations.idiomatic: You write: "My regard for men of promise is old and has its reasons."

sentences.zh: 今伐人之君，啗人以利，真可謂「處懷期物，自有由來」者矣。

translations.literal: Now you attack another's lord and bait men with profit—truly this may be called "my mind toward men of promise has its reasons, long standing."
translations.idiomatic: Now you attack a lord and bait men with gain—that is your "old regard for promise."

sentences.zh: 劉藩死於閶闔之內，諸葛斃於左右之手，甘言詫方伯，襲之以輕兵，遂使席上靡款懷之士，閫外無自信諸侯，以是為得算，良可恥也。

translations.literal: Liu Fan died within the palace gates; Zhuge perished at the hands of those beside him. Sweet words deceived the regional lords, and light troops struck them—so that at the feast there were no men of open heart, and beyond the gate no lords who trusted themselves. To call this good strategy is truly shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan died inside the palace; Zhuge at a neighbor's hand. Flattery fooled the lords, then light troops struck—no open hearts at court, no confident lords abroad. To call that strategy is shame.

sentences.zh: 貴府將佐及朝廷賢德，寄性命以過日，心企太平久矣。

translations.literal: Your staff and the worthy of the court stake their lives day by day and long for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Your staff and the court's worthies stake their lives and long for peace.

sentences.zh: 吾誠鄙劣，嘗聞道於君子。

translations.literal: I am indeed base and inferior, yet I have heard the Way from gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: I am base, yet I have heard the Way from gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 以平西之至德，寧可無授命之臣乎！

translations.literal: With the Pacifier of the West's utmost virtue, could there be no minister who would receive his command?
translations.idiomatic: With such virtue in the Pacifier of the West, can there be no man to die for him?

sentences.zh: 未能自投虎口，比迹郗、任之徒明矣。

translations.literal: That I cannot throw myself into the tiger's maw is clearer than the likeness to Xi and Ren.
translations.idiomatic: That I will not leap into the tiger's mouth is clearer than my likeness to Xi and Ren.

sentences.zh: 假令天長喪亂，九流渾濁，當與臧洪遊於地下，不復多言。

translations.literal: If chaos should long endure and the nine streams grow turbid, I shall wander underground with Zang Hong and say no more.
translations.idiomatic: If chaos endures and the world grows foul, I will keep Zang Hong company underground—and say no more.

sentences.zh: 公視書歎息，以示諸佐曰：「事人當如此。」

translations.literal: Gaozu read the letter and sighed, showing it to his aides and saying: "To serve a man should be like this."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read the letter, sighed, and showed it to his staff: "This is how one should serve."

sentences.zh: 三月，軍次江陵。

translations.literal: In the third month the army halted at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the army reached Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初雍州刺史魯宗之常慮不為公所容，與休之相結，至是率其子竟陵太守軌會于江陵。

translations.literal: Earlier the Inspector of Yongzhou Lu Zongzhi had often feared he would not be tolerated by Gaozu and had joined with Xiuzhi; now he led his son Gui, Administrator of Jingling, to join Xiuzhi at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi of Yong had feared Gaozu would not spare him and had joined Xiuzhi; now he brought his son Gui, Jingling's governor, to meet Xiuzhi at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 江夏太守劉虔之邀之，軍敗見殺。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Jiangxia Liu Qianzhi intercepted them; their army was defeated and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxia's Liu Qianzhi intercepted them; their force was beaten and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 公命彭城內史徐逵之、參軍王允之出江夏口，復為軌所敗，並沒。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered the Interior Minister of Pengcheng Xu Daizhi and staff officer Wang Yunzhi out toward the Jiangxia mouth; they were again defeated by Gui and both perished.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Pengcheng's Xu Daizhi and Wang Yunzhi to the Jiangxia mouth; Gui beat them and both fell.

sentences.zh: 時公軍泊馬頭，即日率眾軍濟江，躬督諸將登岸，莫不奮踊爭先。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu's army was moored at Matou; that same day he led the hosts across the river, personally directing the generals ashore; none failed to leap forward and strive to be first.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's fleet lay at Matou. That day he crossed the river and led the landing himself; every man strove to be first.

sentences.zh: 休之眾潰，與軌等奔襄陽，江陵平。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's troops collapsed; with Gui and others he fled to Xiangyang, and Jiangling was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's army broke; he fled with Gui to Xiangyang. Jiangling was pacified.

sentences.zh: 加領南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Pacification Commissioner for the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Pacification Commissioner for the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 將拜，值四廢日，佐史鄭鮮之、褚叔度、王弘、傅亮白遷日，不許。

translations.literal: When he was about to take office, it fell on a day of the four prohibitions; the clerks Zheng Xianzhi, Chu Shudu, Wang Hong, and Fu Liang reported that the day should be changed, but this was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office it was a forbidden day; Zheng Xianzhi and others asked to move the date, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：「此州積弊，事故相仍，民疲田蕪，杼軸空匱。

translations.literal: An edict was issued, saying: "This province has long accumulated abuses; incidents follow one another in succession; the people are weary and the fields lie waste; the loom's axle and the tax rolls are empty.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "This province is worn by abuses; the people are tired and fields lie waste; coffers are empty.

sentences.zh: 加以舊章乖昧，事役頻苦，童耄奪養，老稚服戎，空戶從役，或越紼應召。

translations.literal: Moreover old regulations are confused and unclear, corvée and service are frequent and bitter; the very young are robbed of nurture, old and young bear arms; empty households are pressed into service, and some cross the mourning cord to answer summons.
translations.idiomatic: Laws are tangled; labor is harsh. Children lose their keep; old and young bear arms. Empty households are drafted; some leave mourning to serve.

sentences.zh: 每永懷民瘼，宵分忘寢，誠宜蠲除苛政，弘茲簡惠。

translations.literal: Whenever I long think of the people's afflictions I forget sleep at midnight; it is truly fitting to abolish harsh government and extend this simple kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When I think of the people's pain I cannot sleep. Harsh rule must go; simple mercy must spread.

sentences.zh: 庶令凋風弊政，與事而新，寧一之化，成於朞月。

translations.literal: May declining winds and corrupt policies be made new with the affair; the transformation of peace and unity be accomplished within a month.
translations.idiomatic: May rotten custom turn new; may peace come within a month.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍二州，西局、蠻府吏及軍人年十二以還，六十以上，及扶養孤幼，單丁大艱，悉仰遣之。

translations.literal: In Jing and Yong, clerks of the western bureau and the barbarian headquarters and soldiers aged twelve and above and sixty and below, and those rearing orphans and the young, sole survivors in great hardship—all are to be sent home as relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing and Yong, clerks, barbarian-office staff, and soldiers from twelve to sixty, and those raising orphans or alone in hardship—all are released.

sentences.zh: 窮獨不能存者，給其長賑。

translations.literal: Those destitute and alone who cannot survive shall be given long-term relief.
translations.idiomatic: The destitute who cannot live shall receive long relief.

sentences.zh: 府州久勤將吏，依勞銓序。

translations.literal: Officers and clerks of the headquarters and province who have long toiled in military affairs shall be ranked in order according to their labor.
translations.idiomatic: Long-serving officers shall be promoted by merit.

sentences.zh: 并除今年租稅。」

translations.literal: This year's land tax is also remitted."
translations.idiomatic: This year's taxes are remitted."

sentences.zh: 四月，公復率眾進討，至襄陽，休之奔羌。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Gaozu again led the hosts forward in punitive campaign, reaching Xiangyang; Xiuzhi fled to the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Gaozu marched again to Xiangyang; Xiuzhi fled to the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 天子復重申前命，授太傅、揚州牧，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，加前部羽葆、鼓吹，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again reiterated the former command, appointing Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, sword and shoes in the hall, no hurrying in court entry, no naming in congratulatory bows, adding the former feathered canopy, drums, and whistles, and setting four Left and Right Chiefs of Staff, Marshals, and Attending Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again offered Grand Tutor and Yangzhou, sword in hall, no hurry in court, no name in bows, canopy and drums, and four chiefs of staff and attendants.

sentences.zh: 封公第三子義隆為北彭城縣公。

translations.literal: Gaozu's third son Yilong was enfeoffed as Duke of North Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Yilong was made Duke of North Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 以中軍將軍道憐為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Central Army General Dao Lin was made Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Lin, Central Army General, became Jingzhou's inspector.

sentences.zh: 八月甲子，公至自江陵，奉還黃鉞，固辭太傅、州牧、前部羽葆、鼓吹，其餘受命。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi in the eighth month Gaozu arrived from Jiangling, returned the yellow battle-axe, and firmly declined Grand Tutor, Governor, the former canopy, drums, and whistles; the rest he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi in the eighth month Gaozu returned from Jiangling, gave back the yellow axe, and refused Grand Tutor, Yangzhou, canopy and drums; he took the rest.

sentences.zh: 朝議以公道尊勳重，不宜復施敬護軍，既加殊禮，奏事不復稱名。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that Gaozu's way was honored and his merit weighty and that respect should no longer be shown the Protector Army; since extraordinary rites had been added, memorials no longer used his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: The court held his merit too great for ordinary titles; memorials no longer named him.

sentences.zh: 以世子為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: The Heir was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made Yanzhou's inspector.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，詔公依舊辟士。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year an edict ordered Gaozu to recruit scholars as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year he was ordered to recruit scholars as before.

sentences.zh: 加領平北將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made General Who Pacifies the North and Yanzhou's inspector.

sentences.zh: 增都督南秦，凡二十二州。

translations.literal: His area supervision was increased by Southern Qin, twenty-two provinces in all.
translations.idiomatic: His supervision was extended to Southern Qin—twenty-two provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 公以平北文武寡少，不宜別置。

translations.literal: Gaozu held that the civil and military staff of Pacify the North were few and that a separate establishment should not be set up.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu judged the Pacify-the-North staff too small for a separate office.

sentences.zh: 於是罷平北府，以併大府。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Pacify the North headquarters was abolished and merged into the great headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the Pacify-the-North office and merged it into his own.

sentences.zh: 以世子為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The Heir was made Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: The heir became Yu province's inspector.

sentences.zh: 三月，加公中外大都督。

translations.literal: In the third month Gaozu was additionally appointed Grand Commander Within and Without.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was made Grand Commander Within and Without.

sentences.zh: 初公平齊，仍有定關、洛之意，值盧循侵逼，故其事不諧。

translations.literal: When Gaozu had first pacified Qi he still intended to settle the passes and Luoyang, but Lu Xun's invasion forced the plan aside.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Qi he still meant to take the passes and Luoyang, but Lu Xun's raid put that off.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍既平，方謀外略。

translations.literal: With Jing and Yong pacified, he turned to plans for external conquest.
translations.idiomatic: With Jing and Yong secure, he planned outward conquest.

sentences.zh: 會羌主姚興死，子泓立，兄弟相殺，關中擾亂，公乃戒嚴北討。

translations.literal: It happened that the Qiang ruler Yao Xing died and his son Hong succeeded; brothers killed one another and Guanzhong was in turmoil, and Gaozu thereupon ordered the army to muster for northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing of the Qiang died; his son Hong succeeded and brothers slew each other. Guanzhong fell into chaos, and Gaozu mustered the north.

sentences.zh: 加領征西將軍、司豫二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of Si and Yu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made General Who Campaigns West and inspector of Si and Yu.

sentences.zh: 以世子為徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: The Heir was made Inspector of Xu and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The heir took Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：「吾倡大義，首自本州，克復皇祚，遂建勳烈，外夷勍敵，內清姦軌，皆邦人州黨竭誠盡力之效也。

translations.literal: An edict was issued, saying: "I raised the great cause, first from this province, restored the imperial house, and thus built meritorious achievement; foreign barbarians and fierce enemies abroad, traitors and villains within—all are the effect of the men of our province and district exhausting their sincerity and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered: "I raised the righteous cause from this province, restored the throne, and built merit. Foes abroad and traitors within—all owe our province's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 情若風霜，義貫金石。

translations.literal: Feeling is like frost and wind; righteousness pierces metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Our feeling is frost and wind; our righteousness cuts metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 今當奉辭西斾，有事關、河，弱嗣叨蒙，復忝今授，情事纏綿，可謂深矣。

translations.literal: Now, as I take leave west with the army, there is business in the passes and the Yellow River; my young heir presumptuously receives this present appointment—the ties of feeling are deep indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Now I march west to the passes and the River; my young heir takes this post—the bond runs deep.

sentences.zh: 頃軍國務殷，刑辟未息，眷言懷之，能不多歎。

translations.literal: Recently military and state affairs have been pressing and punishments have not ceased; whenever I think of this my sighs are many.
translations.idiomatic: War and state affairs press; punishments have not ceased. I sigh whenever I think of it.

sentences.zh: 其犯罪繫五歲以還，可一原遣。

translations.literal: Those guilty of crimes imprisoned for five years and back may all be pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners of five years or less may all be freed.

sentences.zh: 文武勞滿未蒙榮轉者，便隨班序報。」

translations.literal: Civil and military men whose labor is full yet who have not received honorable promotion shall at once be reported in order of rank."
translations.idiomatic: Officers whose service is complete but who lack promotion shall be reported in order."

sentences.zh: 公受中外都督及司州，並辭大司馬琅邪王禮敬，朝議從之。

translations.literal: Gaozu received the commandership within and without and Si province, and also declined the ceremonial deference owed the Prince of Langye, Grand Marshal; court discussion followed his wish.
translations.idiomatic: He took the grand command and Si, and declined ceremonial deference to Prince Langye; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 公欲以義聲懷遠，奉琅邪王北伐。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished to win the distant by righteous reputation and to lead the Prince of Langye north in campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to win the far lands by righteousness and lead Prince Langye north.

sentences.zh: 五月，羌偽黃門侍郎尹沖率兄弟歸順。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the false Qiang Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yin Chong led his brothers in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Qiang pretender Yin Chong and his brothers submitted.

sentences.zh: 又加公北雍州刺史，前部羽葆、鼓吹，增班劍為四十人。

translations.literal: He was again made Inspector of Northern Yong, with the former feathered canopy, drums, and whistles, and his ceremonial swords were increased to forty.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Northern Yong's inspector, with canopy, drums, and forty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 解中書監。

translations.literal: He was relieved of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He left the post of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 八月丁巳，率大眾發京師。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi in the eighth month he led the great host out of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the eighth month he led the great army from the capital.

sentences.zh: 以世子為中軍將軍，監太尉留府事。

translations.literal: The Heir was made Central Army General and supervised the Grand Commandant's headquarters affairs left in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The heir became Central Army General and oversaw the capital headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射劉穆之為左僕射，領監軍、中軍二府軍司，入居東府，總攝內外。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Muzhi was made Left Director, holding the supervisory army and central army headquarters as army clerk, entering the Eastern Headquarters to oversee all within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi became Left Director, supervised the armies, and ran the Eastern Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 九月，公次于彭城，加領徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Gaozu halted at Pengcheng and was additionally made Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he halted at Pengcheng and was also made Xu's inspector.

sentences.zh: 先是遣冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡步向許、洛，羌緣道屯守，皆望風降服。

translations.literal: Earlier he had sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Dragon Cavalry General Wang Zhen'e marching toward Xu and Luoyang; along the road the Qiang garrisoned and guarded, and all looked to the wind and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He had sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen'e toward Xu and Luoyang; Qiang garrisons along the way submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 偽兗州刺史韋華先據倉垣，亦率眾歸順。

translations.literal: The false Inspector of Yanzhou Wei Hua, who had first held Cangyuan, likewise led his host in submission.
translations.idiomatic: The pretender Wei Hua of Yan, holding Cangyuan, also submitted.

sentences.zh: 公又遣北兗州刺史王仲德先以水軍入河。

translations.literal: Gaozu again sent the Inspector of Northern Yanzhou Wang Zhongde ahead with the water army into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Wang Zhongde of Northern Yan ahead with the fleet into the river.

sentences.zh: 仲德破索虜於東郡涼城，進平滑臺。

translations.literal: Zhongde defeated the barbarians of the north at Liangcheng in Dongjun and advanced to pacify Pingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde beat the northern barbarians at Liangcheng and took Pingtai.

sentences.zh: 十月，眾軍至洛陽，圍金墉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the armies reached Luoyang and besieged Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the armies reached Luoyang and besieged Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 泓弟偽平南將軍洸請降，送于京師。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother, the false General Who Pacifies the South Guang, requested surrender and was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's brother Guang, false Pacifier of the South, surrendered and was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 修復晉五陵，置守衞。

translations.literal: The five tombs of Jin were restored and guards were set.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's five tombs were restored and guarded.

sentences.zh: 天子詔曰：

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's edict said:

sentences.zh: 夫嵩、岱配極，則乾道增輝，藩嶽作屏，則帝王成務。

translations.literal: Song and Dai match the pole, then the way of heaven gains brilliance; when frontier mountains serve as screens, then the emperor's task is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Dai crown the pole and heaven shines; frontier mountains screen the throne and the emperor's work is done.

sentences.zh: 是以夏、殷資昆、彭之伯，有周倚齊、晉之輔。

translations.literal: Thus Xia and Yin relied on the lords Kun and Peng; Zhou leaned on the assists of Qi and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Xia and Yin had Kun and Peng; Zhou had Qi and Jin.

sentences.zh: 鑒諸前典，儀刑萬代，翼治扶危，靡不由此。

translations.literal: Looking to the former canon, the model for ten thousand generations—aiding rule and supporting the endangered—none is not through this.
translations.idiomatic: The old canon shows it: aiding rule and saving the realm—none without such lords.

sentences.zh: 太尉公命世天縱，齊聖廣淵，明燭四方，道光宇宙。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant's fate fills the age, his sagacity is broad and deep, his illumination lights the four quarters, his way shines through the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant is heaven's child, broad and deep, lighting the four quarters, his way filling the cosmos.

sentences.zh: 爰自□□初迪，則投懃王國，妖蝥孔熾，則功存社稷。

translations.literal: From the beginning of the restoration he threw his diligence into the royal house; when the demonic locusts burned fiercely, his merit preserved the altars.
translations.idiomatic: From the restoration he served the throne; when rebellion raged, his merit saved the altars.

sentences.zh: 固以四維是荷，萬邦攸賴者矣。

translations.literal: Thus he bears the four bonds and all states rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: He bears the realm's pillars; all states lean on him.

sentences.zh: 暨桓玄僭逆，傾蕩四海，公深秉大節，靈武霆震，弘濟朕躬，再造王室。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped and rebelled, overturning the four seas, Gaozu deeply held the great principle; his martial spirit thundered; he broadly rescued Our person and remade the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan usurped and shook the realm, Gaozu held fast to right; his thunderous might rescued the throne and remade the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 每惟勳德，銘于厥心，遂北清海、岱，南夷百越，荊、雍稽服，庸、岷順軌，剋黜方難，式遏寇虐。

translations.literal: Whenever I think of his merit and virtue I inscribe it in my heart; then he cleared the sea and Mount Tai in the north and subdued the hundred Yue in the south; Jing and Yong bowed in submission; Yong and Min followed the track; he overcame regional difficulties and checked bandits and cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: His merit is carved in my heart: he cleared north and south, won Jing and Yong, checked rebels and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 及阿衡王猷，班序內外，仰興絕風，傍嗣逸業。

translations.literal: As he balanced the royal plan and ordered inner and outer ranks, he raised the fallen wind and continued the lost enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered court and realm, revived fallen custom, and continued lost work.

sentences.zh: 秉禮以整俗，遵王以垂訓，聲教遠被，無思不洽。

translations.literal: Upholding rites to rectify custom, following the king to hand down instruction—his sound and teaching spread far; none thought was left unpervaded.
translations.idiomatic: By rites he ordered custom; by the king's way he taught—his fame reached far; none was untouched.

sentences.zh: 爰暨木居海處之酋，被髮彫題之長，莫不忘其陋險，九譯來庭，此蓋播諸徽策，靡究其詳者也。

translations.literal: Even chiefs who dwelt in trees by the sea and leaders with tattooed foreheads and shaved hair did not forget their rough peril; through nine translations they came to court—this is broadly set forth in glorious records, though the detail cannot be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Even tree-dwelling chiefs and tattooed lords forgot their hardship and came through nine interpreters to court—this the records praise beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 曩者永嘉不綱，諸夏幅裂，終古帝居，淪胥戎虜，永言園陵，率土同慕。

translations.literal: Formerly in the Yongjia disorder the threads of rule were broken and the many Xia split apart; the imperial dwelling of old was lost to barbarian captivity; speaking of the imperial tombs, all the land shared the same longing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjia's ruin the realm split; the old capital fell to barbarians; all the land mourned the tombs.

sentences.zh: 公明發遐慨，撫機電征，親董侯伯，稜威致討。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent forth distant indignation, seized the moment and marched with lightning speed, personally directing the marquis and lords, his awl-edge authority bringing punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu burned with distant wrath, seized the moment, and marched; he led the lords himself.

sentences.zh: 旗旝首塗，則八表響震；

translations.literal: When the banners took the first road, the eight regions trembled in response;
translations.idiomatic: When the banners moved first, the eight regions shook;

sentences.zh: 偏師先路，則多壘雲徹。

translations.literal: when the detached army led the way, many ramparts fell like clouds parting.
translations.idiomatic: when the vanguard went ahead, ramparts fell like clouds.

sentences.zh: 舊都載清，五陵復禮，百城屈膝，千落影從。

translations.literal: The old capital was cleared, the five tombs received rites again; a hundred cities bent the knee and a thousand settlements followed in shadow.
translations.idiomatic: The old capital was cleared; the five tombs were honored; cities bowed and settlements followed.

sentences.zh: 自篇籍所載，生民以來，勳德懋功，未有若此之盛者也。

translations.literal: From what the records carry, since living men began, in meritorious virtue and majestic achievement nothing has equaled this splendor.
translations.idiomatic: In all the records, since men began, no merit has matched this splendor.

sentences.zh: 昔周、呂佐叡聖之主，因三分之形，把旄仗鉞，一時指麾，皆大啟疆宇，跨州兼國。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhou and Lü assisted sage rulers; because of the shape of the three divisions they held staffs and battle-axes; for a time they directed, and all greatly opened frontier territory and spanned provinces and states.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Lü aided sage kings, held axe and staff, and opened great realms across provinces.

sentences.zh: 其在桓、文，方茲尤儉，然亦顯被寵章，光錫殊品。

translations.literal: Even in the age of Duke Huan and Duke Wen it was still more restrained, yet they too clearly received favoring seals and were brightly granted special ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Even Duke Huan and Duke Wen received less, yet they won special honors.

sentences.zh: 況乃獨絕百代，顧邈前烈者哉！

translations.literal: How much more does he stand alone for a hundred generations and look down on the heroes of old!
translations.idiomatic: How much more one who stands alone for a hundred generations above the heroes of old!

sentences.zh: 朕每弘鑒古訓，思遵令圖。

translations.literal: Whenever I broadly mirror the ancient instruction I think to follow the present chart.
translations.idiomatic: I mirror the ancients and seek the present chart.

sentences.zh: 以公深秉沖挹，用闕大禮，天人引領，于茲歷載。

translations.literal: Because Gaozu deeply holds modest restraint, the great rites have been left vacant; heaven and men stretch their necks—thus for years.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu is modest; the great rites wait; heaven and men have watched for years.
